judgements.justification: A's AC called the paper 'generally solid' with 'reasonably strong' results but rejected it as 'still slightly below' the bar on a 5.4 mean.
A's Reviewer_Tk2H kept 5 over the Gaussian-prior variant, which the method does not use, after the authors posted a three-model table and an alpha sweep.
Both committees read the paper as an auxiliary loss for vision transformers and asked the same shared questions (ImageNet-1K, ResNet, longer training, lambda).
No score moved in either committee after the rebuttal.
A probed the reliability of the same evidence harder, but neither committee required a deliverable the other did not ask for.
G9ps misdescribed the setting as fine-tuning, but no reviewer's praise or score rested on a wrong claim about novelty or results.
No below-threshold reviewer said the rebuttal resolved its main concern: ndSd said its main concerns remain, Tk2H held its point, Z3Px stayed unconvinced.
Both committees received the same actual rebuttal experiments; neither split on crediting promised revisions.
K16j called the rebuttal 'somewhat positive but high uncertainty' and kept 6, a stance consistent with its score; no reviewer stated a changed position.
Neither AC called in an additional off-record reviewer.
Both committees found the paper clearly written; clarity was not a point of difference.
No reviewer raised a score; no review was edited after the rebuttal except cpF3's, which kept its 6.
A's AC counted its three silent reviewers, and B's AC set aside no rating for silence.
The highest rating was A's jUVG 7, one point above threshold and carrying its own doubts; no reviewer championed the paper well above threshold.
No reviewer in either committee admitted reading only part of the paper.
No reviewer contested the premise from a different theoretical tradition.
B's meta-review gave a spotlight over 6, 6, 5, 6 with no reviewer above 6 and gave no reason for the award tier.
The split was in scrutiny of runs, test-set selection and hyperparameters, not in one committee's knowledge of baseline literature.
A's meta-review matches its record; B's misstated consensus on novelty runs toward its higher decision, not a lower one.
No narrow-audience objection capped a tier; K16j's 'narrow applicability' was in B, which gave the spotlight.
No detractor's misreading pushed either AC into arguing only for acceptance.
A-only results (five-seed rerun, learning-rate sweep) raised no score, and both committees got the same core experiments.
A's confidence-5 jUVG rated 7 but itself doubted the single-run evidence, and A's other reviewers, including 20-hour Tk2H, were not less informed.
Z3Px's late comment of 2021-09-03 was answered by the authors the same day, and no score changed late.
A's lower ratings rest on more confirmed concerns (single runs, test-set selection, default hyperparameters), not on a harsher scale for the same assessments.
Neither committee judged the headline claim or title overstated.
B's flat 6s came from confident reviewers (confidence 4 to 5) and B still gave a spotlight; no committee converged on 6 out of uncertainty.
